html:
Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn are Bronze Age sites in the interior of Oman, from the third millennium BCE, with stone towers and rows of beehive-shaped tombs along the ridges.

The tombs, built of stacked stone, held many burials each. The round towers, perhaps forts or water stores, stood by the fields. They belong to the time when the land, known as Magan, traded copper to Sumer.

The sites became a World Heritage Site in 1988, one of the first in Arabia. The tombs on the skyline at Al-Ayn, with the Jebel Misht behind, have become one of the best known images of Oman. Compare the Umm an-Nar tombs of the UAE.
